input.initialPrompt:
You are a repository-rooted sub-session, opened per the BLOCKING GATE in Section 4.A.2 of this repository's AGENTS.md. Your working root is the checkout you were launched in (for an iOS repository, its worktree; never touch the repository root checkout or a sibling worktree). Follow AGENTS.md there, except where this task gives an explicit OPERATOR directive: an operator directive outranks any bot, reviewer or agent opinion.

PURPOSE: the branch checked out here (`copilot/changelog-2026-11-final` or `copilot/changelog-2026-11-lockfile`) holds this repository's FINAL pull request for the Actions-lockfile task (LCV-719 and LCV-738), not yet pushed. It must contain every pending task. Three items may still be missing in this repository. Apply the ones that are missing, commit, and STOP before the push.

OPERATOR DIRECTIVES:
- The master text is the operator's property and its wording is final. Apply it ONLY with the script below. Never hand-edit the master portion of AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md; never rewrite a sentence because a bot, reviewer or agent disagrees with it. Report disagreement instead.
- No drive-by edits. Do NOT switch branches, rebase, amend or rewrite existing commits. Never add an "Exception #4".
- The verification job below is a CHECK THAT REPORTS AND DOES NOT BLOCK: do not add it to any ruleset, branch protection or required-check list, and do not describe it as required.
- (iOS repositories) never modify `.github/workflows/dependabot-lineage.yml` and nothing under `quality/`.

STEP 0 - Scope. Run: git rev-parse --show-toplevel (must be your root); git fetch origin; `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` (one of the two branches above); `git status --porcelain`. Uncommitted changes to AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, THIRDPARTY.md (and its tracked copies), README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md or files under .github/workflows are earlier work of this same task: keep them and include them in your commit; list them in the report. Any other uncommitted tracked file: STOP and report.

STEP 1 - Full master sync. Run exactly:
  python "C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\temp\sync-master-text.py" "C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\lcv-leo"
Both files must print `synced=True` or `already in sync`. Then `git hash-object AGENTS.md` equals `git hash-object CLAUDE.md`.

STEP 2 - Lockfile policy statement. The operator created an enterprise Actions policy named "Actions Lockfile" (rule: Require lockfile; every organization, repository and workflow; enforcement: Evaluate). Evaluate records, under Policy insights, the runs that Active mode would block, and blocks none. In the CHANGELOG Unreleased section, find the clause stating that the `Require lockfile` policy stays off (English: "stays off", "remains off", "continues disabled"; Portuguese: "permanece desligada", "continua desativada", "segue desligada") and replace ONLY that clause, grammatical in its own language:
  - English: "The `Require lockfile` policy runs in **Evaluate** mode at the enterprise."
  - Portuguese: "A política `Require lockfile` roda em modo **Evaluate** no enterprise."
Do the same in any README, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY or THIRDPARTY sentence carrying that statement. If nothing carries it, change nothing and say so. Dated historical CHANGELOG entries stay.

STEP 3 - Verification job. Create `.github/workflows/verify-lockfile.yml` with exactly this content:

name: verify-lockfile

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: github/gh-actions-lock@5fa07d19c267d19e29f4341f10fdf7f516375038 # verify/v0.5.1

This is the official example of the `github/gh-actions-lock` repository (README and verify/README.md). Exactly two adaptations are allowed, and only when the repository already uses a different convention in its other workflows:
  (a) `runs-on`: the runner label this repository's other Linux jobs use; otherwise keep `ubuntu-latest`.
  (b) permissions: `permissions: {}` at the top level and `permissions: contents: read` on the job; the effective grant must stay `contents: read`.
Nothing else changes: no path filter, no `paths-ignore`, no push trigger, no extra inputs, no `continue-on-error`. Write `verify/v0.5.1` as the version (the tag `verify/v*` is the one the documentation says to pin). Match the file's indentation style of the repository's other workflows only if it differs (spaces); the content above is already the YAML the documentation shows.
If `.github/workflows/verify-lockfile.yml` already exists on this branch, verify it equals this content and skip the creation.

STEP 4 - Onboard the new workflow. Run `gh actions-lock --no-narrow` (never a plain run: a plain run rewrites every full-SHA pin into a mutable tag). It must add the new workflow and its two dependencies to `.github/workflows/actions.lock`. Then prove: `git diff --name-only origin/main -- .github/workflows/` lists only `actions.lock`, `verify-lockfile.yml` and, on a branch that introduces the lockfile itself, nothing else; no existing `.yml` changed; `gh actions-lock --verify` reports all workflows valid; zizmor over `.github/workflows` in offline mode exits 0. (iOS) `dependabot-lineage.yml` and `quality/` are untouched.

STEP 5 - Documentation surfaces of the new job.
  a. Inventory. Where THIRDPARTY.md (and each tracked copy of it) lists the GitHub Actions this repository runs, add `github/gh-actions-lock` (the action named "Verify actions.lock"), version `verify/v0.5.1`, commit `5fa07d19c267d19e29f4341f10fdf7f516375038`, MIT, license link https://github.com/github/gh-actions-lock/blob/5fa07d19c267d19e29f4341f10fdf7f516375038/LICENSE , used by `.github/workflows/verify-lockfile.yml` on every pull request. Follow the file's row or prose convention; keep tracked copies byte-identical.
  b. Workflow lists. Where a README, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY or docs section enumerates this repository's workflows or its pull-request checks, add the new workflow as a check that runs on every pull request and reports without blocking. Where nothing enumerates workflows, add nothing.
  c. CHANGELOG. Add ONE Unreleased entry, in this repository's language, stating: the repository now runs the official `verify-lockfile` workflow on every pull request through `github/gh-actions-lock`, which fails when `actions.lock` is out of sync with the workflows or a locked pin no longer verifies upstream; it reports and does not block, because it is not a required check (LCV-738).

STEP 6 - Mechanical checks. Set TMP, TEMP and TMPDIR to a temp/ folder inside this checkout first. Run each and paste its output:
  & "C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\temp\sweep-versions.ps1" -Root "C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\lcv-leo"     -> VERSION-SWEEP CLEAN
  & "C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\temp\check-inventory.ps1" -Root "C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\lcv-leo"    -> no MISSING-FROM-INVENTORY line
  & "C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\temp\verify-claims.ps1" -Root "C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\lcv-leo"       -> CLEAN
  gh actions-lock --verify                                                             -> all workflows valid
Then every local gate this repository defines that reads the files this branch changed: the exact commands CI runs (from .github/workflows/ci.yml, package.json or the build files), including any test that reads the workflows or the documentation. iOS: never run Xcode or simulators; declare them as validation gaps. When a gate exits non-zero, classify it: caused by this branch (fix it), pre-existing at the base (prove by stash and re-run; out of scope), or environmental (prove which; validation gap). Never report a gate as passed when it did not run or did not pass.

STEP 7 - Commit. `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` must equal `git rev-parse origin/main`. Write the message to temp/commit-msg.txt (Conventional Commits, US English, the trailer `Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>` as the last line). Suggested title: `ci(lockfile): verify actions.lock on every pull request and sync the workspace instructions`. The body states what you did in steps 1 to 5. `git add` each changed file by name (never temp/). Commit with `git commit -S -F temp/commit-msg.txt`. Verify with `git log -1 --format=%B` that the `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer exists and with `git for-each-ref "refs/entire/checkpoints/**"` that its ref exists locally. Never pass --no-verify. Never run `entire session attach`.

STEP 8 - STOP. Do not push, do not open a pull request, do not create temp/pr-body.md.

REPORT (short): branch; `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD`; `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`; which of the three items were missing and what you did for each; the new workflow file content if you adapted it; the lockfile entries added; the mechanical check outputs; every gate with its exit code; anything out of scope you noticed and did NOT touch.


======================================================================
RESUME ADDENDUM. This session RESUMES an earlier one that was killed from outside while working in this checkout, before it could commit. Where this addendum and the task above differ, the addendum prevails.

R1. Working tree. The uncommitted changes you find are that earlier session's work on this same task and this same branch. Keep them: read `git status --porcelain` and `git diff`, finish what is incomplete, correct what is wrong, and include all of it in your commit. Never discard them: no `git checkout -- <file>`, no `git restore`, no `git reset`, no branch switch, no rebase, no `git clean`. The sentence in STEP 0 that says to STOP on an uncommitted tracked file outside its list does not apply to the files named in R5.

R2. Finish the earlier work FIRST (skip each item that is already complete, and prove it with a command), then run STEPS 1 to 8 above.
  a. Lockfile. `gh actions-lock --verify` must report every workflow valid. Every `uses:` line keeps its full 40-character commit SHA and its version comment. If any was rewritten to a tag, restore that workflow file with `git checkout origin/main -- <file>` and run `gh actions-lock --no-narrow` again. Never a plain `gh actions-lock`.
  b. Inventory. Every file that lists the GitHub Actions this repository runs (THIRDPARTY.md and each tracked copy, `git ls-files "*THIRDPARTY*"`; any README, CONTRIBUTING or SECURITY section that names Action versions) agrees with the live `uses:` pins and with the `dependencies:` section of actions.lock:
     - each directly used Action: the live version, its commit, and a license link that resolves at that commit (check with `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/LICENSE?ref=<sha>`);
     - each transitive-only Action, and each second revision of an Action that a workflow also pins directly: named with the Action that pulls it in, its commit, and a license link at that commit; when a workflow pins the same Action directly at another revision, name both paths;
     - tracked copies byte-identical to their source (`git hash-object`).
     Leave version drift that already exists at the base and that you do not touch, and report it.
  c. Prose. No undated passage of tracked Markdown still declares actions.lock nonexistent, retired or forbidden, and none still says the `Require lockfile` policy is off (STEP 2 above gives the wording). Dated historical CHANGELOG entries stay.
  d. CHANGELOG, Unreleased section. It carries one entry, in this repository's language and style, recording the adoption of the lockfile and the inventory reconciliation and referencing LCV-719. Complete it if it is missing or unfinished. The entry STEP 5c asks for is a separate, additional entry.
  e. Every instruction you write or edit about generating or refreshing the lockfile names `gh actions-lock --no-narrow`.

R3. To prove that a failing gate also fails at the base, STEP 6 allows `git stash`. If you use it: push and pop in the same command, then prove with `git status --porcelain` that the working tree is exactly as before; leave no stash of yours behind (`git stash list`).

R4. Report, before the task's own report: what the earlier session had left unfinished, what you corrected, and every stash entry that existed before you started (do not touch those).

R5. Files outside the task's list that belong in this commit:
None. This repository is a public user-account repository, `lcv-leo/lcv-leo`: pass `--repo lcv-leo/lcv-leo` to every gh command that needs a repository and accepts it; `gh actions-lock` reads the repository from this checkout's remote.

<sql>
**Session database**: persists for this session and is isolated from other sessions. Use it for structured operational data such as todos, test cases, batches, and state.

**Built-in tables:**
- `todos`: id, title, description, status (pending/in_progress/done/blocked), created_at, updated_at
- `todo_deps`: todo_id, depends_on

`todos` and `todo_deps` already exist—insert into them; never create them.

**Todo tracking with dependencies:** Use descriptive kebab-case IDs, gerund titles (for example "Creating user auth module"), and self-contained descriptions. Status meanings:
- `pending`: not started
- `in_progress`: active; set before starting
- `done`: complete
- `blocked`: cannot proceed; explain why in the description

Record every actual prerequisite in `todo_deps`; do not infer dependencies from list order. Before inserting a dependency, insert both todos referenced by its `todo_deps` row. Todos with no prerequisites should remain independent.

Example with two dependent todos, one independent todo, and a ready-todo query:
```sql
-- Todo dependency example
INSERT INTO todos (id, title, description) VALUES
  ('user-model', 'Creating user model', 'Define the User schema and relations in src/models/user.ts'),
  ('api-routes', 'Creating API routes', 'Implement routes that use the User model'),
  ('theme-toggle', 'Adding theme toggle', 'Add an independent dark-mode toggle to the settings page');
INSERT INTO todo_deps (todo_id, depends_on) VALUES ('api-routes', 'user-model');
SELECT t.* FROM todos t
WHERE t.status = 'pending'
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM todo_deps td
    JOIN todos dep ON td.depends_on = dep.id
    WHERE td.todo_id = t.id AND dep.status != 'done'
);
```

Create other tables as needed to load/query data (including CSVs, API responses, and file listings), store structured intermediate results, or manage workflows. Example session state:
```sql
CREATE TABLE session_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO session_state (key, value) VALUES ('current_phase', 'testing');
SELECT value FROM session_state WHERE key = 'current_phase';
```
</sql>

## 4. Mandatory Operational Protocol: Entire + GitHub Enterprise Integration & Anti-Hang PR Flow (`LCV-517` / Ruleset ID `20582436`)

GitHub Enterprise and Entire run in parallel. Entire's architecture ([Entire docs](https://docs.entire.com/)) and the `LCV-517` sequence below are mandatory for full session and checkpoint capture and to keep Pull Requests from hanging on the Enterprise Rulesets ([rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets); `20582436` on `main`, `20613778` on every other branch).

### A. Entire Architecture, Hook Locations, Session Spawning, Crosslinking & Handoff

Entire captures agent sessions through repository-level agent hooks and links them to commits with the `Entire-Checkpoint` and `Entire-Attribution` trailers, stored under `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` or `entire/checkpoints/v1`.

1. **Hook configuration per agent, present before the session starts** (installed with `entire agent add <agent>` by the operator or on the operator's order, as the Cursor hooks were; agents never change hook configuration on their own): Antigravity CLI `.agents/hooks.json` plus the global title-feed wrapper in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` (`entire hooks antigravity title-tee`); Claude Code `.claude/settings.json`; Codex `.codex/hooks.json`; Copilot CLI `.github/hooks/entire.json`; Cursor `.cursor/hooks.json` (operator decision, [Cursor hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks)); external agents `"external_agents": true` in `.entire/settings.local.json`, honored only while that file is untracked (`entire agent-help session attach`). Running agent processes do not load hooks added after they started, and hooks capture only sessions that run inside the Git repository or worktree root where Entire is enabled.

2. **The `lcv-workspace` parent-folder problem.** The operator opens the IDEs at `C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\`, outside any repository root, where Entire's hooks capture nothing.

   > **BLOCKING GATE — Repository-Rooted Sub-Session (operator decision):** before editing any file, staging, or committing in a repository, the agent runs in a session whose working root is that repository's root or that worktree's root. A session started anywhere else opens a sub-session inside that root (commands below) and does the repository work there. The only alternative is Entire's native linking (`entire session adopt` from another worktree, or `entire session attach`, below), only when opening the sub-session is technically impossible, with the raw error recorded as proof. If neither is possible, stop: do not edit, commit, push, or open a Pull Request, and report the proof. Work done in violation of this gate is not delivered work. A sub-session runs the checkout's tracked hooks and configuration at startup, so never open one in a checkout of a branch not created by the operator or the agent (Section 3); review such a branch read-only from the agent's own checkout.

   Binding procedure:
   * Change the working directory to the exact repository root (`C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\<repo>`) or worktree (`C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\.worktrees\<worktree>`), strip inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` ([git environment](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Environment-Variables)), and verify with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` ([git rev-parse](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-parse)).
   * Run `entire status --json` and `entire agent list`. If the agent's hooks are missing or stale, run `entire doctor` for the diagnosis (its offer to fix is declined because the agent's shell is non-interactive) and ask the operator to run `entire agent add <agent> --force`. In a fresh worktree, confirm that the directory named by `git config core.hooksPath` exists (for example `.husky/_`, Git-ignored and created by the repository's install step); without it no hook fires ([githooks](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks)).
   * Spawn the repository-rooted session in that directory: Codex `codex exec "<task>"` or `codex -C <dir> exec "<task>"` ([Codex CLI](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli)); Claude Code `claude -p "<task>" --strict-mcp-config` (never `--bare`, which skips hooks; launch subagents so Entire rolls them into the parent checkpoint) ([Claude Code headless mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless)); GitHub Copilot CLI `copilot -p "<task>" --allow-all --disallow-temp-dir` or `copilot -C <dir> -p "<task>" --allow-all --disallow-temp-dir` (operator decision: a `-p` run denies a tool request that would prompt and, in an untrusted folder, skips the repository hooks; subfolders of a trusted folder are trusted, `copilot help permissions`), or `entire session resume <BRANCH>` / `copilot --resume <SESSION_ID>` ([Copilot CLI programmatic use](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/automate-copilot-cli/run-cli-programmatically), [Entire: Copilot CLI](https://docs.entire.com/agents/copilot-cli)); Cursor: open the repository or worktree itself as the workspace folder; Antigravity `agy` in that directory, or `entire session resume <BRANCH>` / `agy --conversation <SESSION_ID>` ([Antigravity docs](https://antigravity.google/docs)); Antigravity subagent hooks are not attached automatically, so Antigravity work runs in the repo-rooted `agy` session or is linked with `entire session adopt`/`attach` before pushing.
   * **Session identity:** trust `entire session current --json` only when `resolution` is `caller-env` or `ancestry`; `other-worktree` can be any session of the shared store (`entire agent-help session current`).
   * **Adoption (`entire session adopt`):** a session that started in another worktree of the same repository (a worktree that already tracks it; a session started in `lcv-workspace` is not tracked anywhere and uses the crosslinking bullet instead) and continued into the target is adopted before committing: `entire status --json`, then `entire session adopt <SESSION_ID> --from <SOURCE_PATH> --yes` (between worktrees of the same repository, which share one session store, the command requires `--yes` or `--force`, `entire agent-help session adopt`); the next `git commit -S` links it.
   * **Crosslinking (`session-crosslink` protocol):** for a session that ran from `lcv-workspace` or touched several repositories without live capture, resolve the `session_id` (`entire session current --json`, sibling repository state, or `~/.claude/projects/...` / `~/.codex/sessions/...` / `~/.copilot/session-state/...`), inspect each affected repository (`HEAD`, existing `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, `<repo>/.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json`), run `entire session attach <session-id> --agent <agent>` without `--force` in each (it prints its plan), show the plans to the operator, and rerun with `--force` only per confirmed repository, re-verifying the SSH signature on `HEAD` afterwards.
   * **Handoff (`session-handoff` protocol):** when continuing another agent's or session's work, run `entire session current --json` and `entire session list --json`, stream the transcript with `entire session info <id> --transcript`, write the structured handoff (*Task Overview, Current State, Important Discoveries, Next Steps, Context to Preserve, Unanswered Question*), and resume. If `resolution` is neither `caller-env` nor `ancestry`, report the value, do not resume from that session id, and choose the session by its id from `entire session list --json`.

### B. Inviolable Rules of `LCV-517` (Ruleset ID `20582436`)

1. **SSH commit signing:** every commit created locally (`commit`, `amend`, `merge`) is signed with SSH (`git commit -S`, `gpg.format=ssh`, 1Password SSH signer, [1Password Git commit signing](https://www.1password.dev/ssh/git-commit-signing)); never GPG/OpenPGP for your own commits, and never create commits or pull requests through the API from a local session (commits with `git`, pull requests with `gh pr create`, Section 4.C). Unsigned commits fail `required_signatures` ([rules API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules)). The squash commit on `main` is created and signed by GitHub itself (`web-flow`, GitHub's OpenPGP key): that signature is GitHub's, not the operator's, and never a violation of this rule; verify it through the API, `verification.verified == true` ([commits API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/commits), [signature verification](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/about-commit-signature-verification)). `git config user.email` matches the operator's verified GitHub email so `entire.com` never shows `"Unknown author"`.
2. **Conventional Commits** for every message ([Conventional Commits 1.0.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)).
3. **Temporary artifact isolation:** every temporary file stays in `temp/` and is deleted before completion (Section 3).
4. **Entire hooks are never bypassed:** Entire works through `prepare-commit-msg`, `commit-msg`, `post-commit`, `post-rewrite`, and `pre-push` ([githooks](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks)). Never pass `--no-verify` to any `git` command (`-n` in `git commit`; [git commit](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit), [git push](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push)).

### C. Canonical 5-Step Execution & Anti-Hang PR Flow (Exact Certified Order)

Whenever implementing changes and taking a Pull Request to merge, execute these five steps in this order:

* **Step 1: Branch & Development (inside the repository or worktree root)**
  1. Confirm the root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, run `git fetch origin` ([git fetch](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-fetch)), and verify capture with `entire status --json`.
  2. **Branch in the root or worktree (operator decision):** evaluate and state the choice and its reason; never apply one by default. A branch in the root only when the root checkout is clean (`git status --porcelain` empty), on `main`, and not in use by another session or front; preferred for one sequential change and when the repository depends on Git-ignored artifacts of the root (`admin-app`, hooks in `.husky/_`). A worktree when the root has uncommitted work, is in use by another session, must stay on `main` for a live process, or when several changes proceed in parallel; a new worktree contains only tracked files, so confirm its hooks and install artifacts first ([git worktree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree)).
  3. Branch name `<agent>/<task>` with `<agent>` one of `claude`, `codex`, `agy`, `copilot`, `cursor`; Ruleset `20613778` accepts only its live `branch_name_pattern` (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets/20613778`, [rulesets API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules)). Exactly one of: `git checkout -b <agent>/<task> origin/main` in the root ([git checkout](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-checkout)), or `git worktree add C:/Users/lcvle/lcv-workspace/.worktrees/<repo>-<task> -b <agent>/<task> origin/main` followed by the repository-rooted sub-session inside it (Section 4.A.2), from which Step 1.4 through Step 5.3 run.
  4. Implement and validate locally on the project stack in PowerShell, never Git Bash, with every temporary output in `temp/`; a dependency version change is validated by CI instead (Section 3).

* **Step 2: SSH-Signed Commit & Checkpoint Linking**
  1. `git add <files>` (never `temp/`) ([git add](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-add)).
  2. `git commit -S -F temp/commit-msg.txt` — the message in a file, because messages contain backticks ([git commit](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit)).
  3. Confirm the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer with `git log -1 --show-signature --format=fuller` and `entire checkpoint list --json`. If the session was captured (`entire status --json`) but not linked, run `entire session attach <SESSION_ID> --agent <AGENT> --commit <FULL_SHA>` without `--force` first, show its plan to the operator, and rerun with `--force` only after the operator agrees; if `attach` amended the commit, verify that the SSH signature on `HEAD` is still valid.
  4. **Adversarial review before the push (operator decision):** after the commit and before every push that changes content, write `temp/pr-body.md`; a separate reviewer session, spawned in the checkout with the Section 4.A.2 commands, runs the Section 8.B prompts on its review context. Fix each finding in a new signed commit, or disprove it with code evidence or an operator directive in this text and record the disproof in the task's Linear Issue, until a round leaves no finding open; a finding open after three rounds goes to the operator.

* **Step 3: Publication & Pull Request Creation**
  1. `git push -u origin <branch>` (the `pre-push` hook syncs `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`).
  2. `gh pr create --title "<type>(<scope>): <description>" --body-file temp/pr-body.md` ([gh pr create](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_create)).
  3. **Ready for review only, never draft (operator decision):** never `--draft`, never `gh pr ready --undo`, never convert between draft and ready. Each conversion emits the `ready_for_review` or `converted_to_draft` activity of the `pull_request` event, which reruns every workflow subscribed to it and restarts the review bots ([events that trigger workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#pull_request), [gh pr ready](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_ready)); on `astrologo-android` the gates take about one hour, so a draft opened, made ready, and drafted again runs them three times.

* **Step 4: Anti-Hang Handshake (`LCV-517`, mandatory right after `gh pr create`)**
  Run `git commit --amend --no-edit -S` and `git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>` ([git push](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push)). Reason recorded in `LCV-517` (observed behavior, not described in GitHub's documentation): Secret Scanning stays pending (`"Waiting for secret scan to complete..."`) when the first commit was pushed before the Pull Request existed; the amend and force push after creation emit `pull_request.synchronize`, which completes Secret Scanning and triggers CodeQL and Code Quality. Entire keeps the checkpoint link across the amend through `post-rewrite`. Verify with `git ls-remote origin "refs/entire/checkpoints/*" | Select-String -SimpleMatch "<CHECKPOINT_ID>"` ([git ls-remote](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-ls-remote)) in the ref-based layout, or `entire checkpoint list --json` in the `entire/checkpoints/v1` layout, and `git log -1 --show-signature`. The head left by the handshake is the first head under review; from then on Section 5.G, item 4, applies.

* **Step 5: Findings, CI, Merge & Cleanup**
  1. After every push, `gh pr checks <pr> --watch` ([gh pr checks](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_checks)) and `entire trail finding list <repo>/<trail> --freshness any --json` inside the repository checkout (add `--project gh/<project>` only when the project is not origin's owner; 100 per page, continue with `--cursor`; `entire agent-help trail finding list`). Fix real defects and findings, resolve them with `entire trail finding resolve <id> -m "fixed in <sha>"`, and re-verify.

     > **BLOCKING GATE — Active Watch and Zero Open Findings (operator decision):** from the moment a Pull Request or Trail exists until it is merged, keep watching it; bots and the Entire review can post minutes after the checks finish, and every push starts a new round. After each push and again immediately before merging, inventory: review threads, resolved and unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads`, every page, [pull request review threads](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/pulls#object-pullrequestreviewthread)); every review body with its suppressed comments ([reviews API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews)); the conversation comments ([issue comments API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/comments)); Entire Trail findings (`--freshness any`); open diff threads of the linked Linear review; failed or pending checks and code scanning alerts on the head ([code scanning alerts API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning)). **While any finding is open, the Pull Request or Trail is not merged or approved**, whatever the merge button allows. A finding closes only when its code was fixed and the thread or finding is resolved citing the fixing commit, or when it is disproved with evidence from the code or an operator directive in this text and resolved citing that evidence.
  2. `gh pr view <pr> --json mergeStateStatus` ([gh pr view](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_view)).
  3. **The operator merges, or orders the agent to merge (operator decision);** without that order, hand the operator the pull request with every gate clear and the squash body file below. ## 6. Zero-Tolerance Anti-Slop Engineering Protocol, Contract Surface Sweeps & 5-Stage Gatekeeper

"Slop" is avoidable, low-trust work caused by not understanding the repository well enough: unverified assumptions, lazy truncation, hallucinated interfaces, duplicate systems, type evasion and catch-all masking, premature abstraction, unrequested mutation, iteration debris, filler. Any violation below is a critical execution failure.

### A. Anti-Truncation & Complete Implementation
No placeholders, truncation markers, or elisions (`// TODO`, `// FIXME`, `// implement logic here`, `// ... rest of the code`, `/* existing code */`, `pass`). Every code block, script, or patch is complete, syntactically valid, fully imported, and immediately runnable. Never delegate mechanical work to the operator ("repeat this pattern", "add the imports").

### B. Epistemic Anti-Slop
Read the exact live state of a file, function, schema, or workflow and its nearby helpers and tests before writing or referencing it; reuse the repository's established pattern instead of a parallel helper or ad-hoc parser. Never guess library methods, CLI flags, GraphQL fields, environment variables, or SDK signatures: verify against the installed lockfile versions and the official documentation. Never hand-edit or regex a lockfile (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Cargo.lock`); regenerate only with the official tool, in the modes of Section 3.

### C. Architectural, Sequencing & Code Anti-Slop
Strict typing (`strict: true` in TypeScript, strict Python 3.10+ annotations, explicit Go/Rust types); never `any`, `as unknown as T`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `# type: ignore`, or loose `Record<string, any>`: fix the contract. No empty `catch {}`, no log-and-continue that corrupts state, no silent fallbacks (`|| "default"`, `?? 0`) for missing business configuration, credentials, or market prices: fail fast with structured, secret-free logging. No inconsistent, orphaned, or lost state when a later step fails; no irreversible write before a fallible call; cleanup on success and failure; tests use isolated directories or repositories inside `temp/` and never touch the operator's real config, keychain, or checkout. No speculative abstractions, single-implementation interfaces, wrapper classes, or heavy patterns for linear problems: flat, readable, immutable, pure, modular code (SRP, DRY). No accidental $O(N^2)$ loops, N+1 queries, unindexed lookups, unbounded accumulations, or unclosed handles.

### D. Diff Hygiene & Non-Destructive Editing
Modify only the lines and files the task requires; no drive-by refactors, renames, or formatting sweeps; zero iteration debris (dead code, stale comments, unused helpers, abandoned approaches, debug logs). Delete no high-value architectural comment; add no comment that restates the next line, narrates the diff, or explains what the conventions make obvious; comment only the *why* of a non-obvious invariant, security boundary, or business constraint. Preserve encodings and line endings (`core.autocrlf=false`, [git config](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config)); never apply blind global regex replacements to prose or manifests.

### E. Pinned Dependency Bump = 8-Point Contract Surface Sweep

Changing the version of a GitHub Action or pinned dependency is never two files. Follow the `bump-dependencia-pinada` skill (`C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\.claude\skills\bump-dependencia-pinada\SKILL.md`) and sweep all eight surfaces:
1. **Workflow files:** full-SHA pin, version comment, tool-version selection input ([pinning actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use#using-third-party-actions)).
2. **Lockfiles:** as Section 6.B requires. GitHub Actions dependency lockfiles exist and are generally available: `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, generated only by the `gh actions-lock` CLI extension and never edited by hand, refreshed automatically by Dependabot inside the same version-update pull request ([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles), [Locking action dependencies](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/lock-workflow-dependencies)). **Fleet position (operator decision, 25/11/2026):** every repository adopts the Actions lockfile **and keeps its `uses:` references pinned to a full-length commit SHA with the version comment**. GitHub checks the locked commit for an onboarded workflow and a lockfile satisfies the SHA-pinning policy by itself, so the in-file SHA is the fleet's reviewed record, not the enforcement point; keep it so the reviewed pin survives deletion of the lockfile and stays readable in review ([Governing execution of GitHub Actions workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/administer/control-workflow-execution#require-lockfile)). Generate and refresh with **`gh actions-lock --no-narrow`**; a plain run rewrites the pins to version tags and is forbidden here. The **Require lockfile** policy stays off (same page). The extension locks external actions and the actions a `$/` path uses. A local path action (`uses: ./…`) runs whatever is checked out in the runner's workspace, so the extension can neither pin it nor see what it uses. When such an action uses other actions, the extension stops with a `local-action` error before writing the lockfile, so take one of the two documented decisions — `--migrate-local-actions`, which rewrites the reference to the inherently pinned `uses: $/…` form, or an explicit `--ignore-local-actions` — and record which one in the pull request ([Locking action dependencies](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/lock-workflow-dependencies)). A `$/` path runs at the workflow's own commit and is pinned by that commit. A routine `--no-narrow` change touches `actions.lock` only, but upstream renames and transfers rewrite `uses:` names and `--migrate-local-actions` edits workflows, so read the full diff. Every lockfile change still sweeps all eight surfaces of this section. The lockfile does not cover reusable-workflow calls (`jobs.<job_id>.uses`): a cross-repository call stays pinned by full commit SHA, while a same-repository `$/` or `./` call carries no `@ref` and runs at the caller's own commit ([Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax)). A Wrangler update also regenerates `worker-configuration.d.ts` under the Section 3 exception and commits it before pushing.
3. **Repository Actions allowlist:** may pin the exact commit SHA; inspect repository by repository and admit the new commit alongside the old one before merging ([allowed actions](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/permissions#set-allowed-actions-and-reusable-workflows-for-a-repository)).
4. **`THIRDPARTY.md`:** inventory and exception sections whose premise no longer exists.
5. **`README.md`:** version references, prose, anchors to removed sections.
6. **Contract tests and scripts:** `.mjs`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.cjs`, including regex-escaped versions and structural lines such as `ref: "v0.16.0"`.
7. **`CHANGELOG.md`:** the `Unreleased` section (active contract surface).
8. **License, terms, and defaults of the new version:** release notes and, when present, `LICENSE`, `licenses/`, `DISTRIBUTION.md`; a version can switch a default to a proprietary or paid component with no file of ours changing (`gradle/actions` v6 made the closed-source `enhanced` cache the default); any new charge, restriction, or term change stops the bump and goes to the operator.
* **Execution rules:** no regex over prose; the new version is never installed, built, or tested locally except under the Section 3 Wrangler exception, and no local suite runs on the bumped checkout (CI runs it, Section 3 and Step 1.4 of Section 4.C); prepare the change on the checkout of Step 1.3 with `core.autocrlf=false`, inspect the diff, then publish through Section 4.C.

### F. Mandatory 5-Stage Validation Gatekeeper & Pre-Output Self-Audit

Before delivering code or releasing a Pull Request, pass all five stages with concrete proof: (1) principal architectural review (flaws, coupling, anti-patterns, partial-failure corruption); (2) AppSec sweep (SQL injection, command injection, path traversal, XSS, CSRF, broken authentication/authorization, cross-tenant access, unsafe deserialization, sensitive data exposure, insecure dependencies); (3) performance and clean code ($O(N^2)$, needless loops, unindexed queries, leaks, dead code, cyclomatic complexity, naming); (4) QA test truthfulness and edge cases (failure paths, boundaries, races, invalid inputs; implement the mandatory unit or integration tests whose assertions prove the new behavior, not mock echoes); (5) strict specification alignment with the operator's requirements and the prohibitions of Section 5.

**Pre-output self-audit (fail-closed):** before emitting any response, patch, or review, answer internally — (1) is the code 100% complete, with zero `TODO`s, elisions, or unverified APIs? (2) are types strict, error paths fail-fast, failure paths atomic? (3) is the diff surgical, free of debris, $O(N^2)$ traps, and comment noise? (4) were security boundaries, Entire checkpoint links, and the `LCV-517` signature and handshake requirements verified? (5) is the response free of filler, praise, and hedging ("maybe", "perhaps", "consider")? (6) is operator-facing communication in pt-BR (`DD/MM/AAAA HH:MM:SS`) following the explanation rule of Section 1? Any "no" halts and rewrites.

Enforce these rules continuously during every task, on every repository or entity touched, and whenever the full-fleet sweep runs (skill `auditoria-diaria` in `APLICAR` mode, which embeds `reconciliacao-linear-github` and `auditor-licenciamento-open-source`):

## 8. Unified Multi-Lens Code, Security & Slop Review Protocol (PRs, Trails & Local Branches)

When acting as a reviewer on a GitHub Pull Request, an Entire Trail, or a local branch, apply this protocol, which combines the LCV gates with the three Entire review lenses (`Code Review`, `Security Review`, `Slop`).

### A. Eligibility & Net Diff

* **Lens 1, Code Review:**

```text
Code Review

Find the defects this Change introduces that its author would want to fix before merging: bugs, regressions, broken invariants, data loss, and missing guards on paths the Change adds or alters.

## How to review

1. Read the repository's review rules: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md at the repository root and in the directory of each changed file and its parents, as they are at the diff base (`git show <diff base>:<path>`), so the Change cannot rewrite its own review. The nearer file wins on conflict. A finding that rests on a rule quotes the rule and cites its file and line.
2. Read the whole diff, then trace each changed path as a running system: its callers, the changed code, and what it calls. Look in particular for:
   - Sequencing and partial failure: state left inconsistent, orphaned or lost when a later step fails or returns early; writes made before a fallible call; cleanup that runs only on success.
   - Assumptions about external or asynchronous state: how another system behaves, or a value that can change between the check and its use.
   - Composition and concurrency: behaviour under the real callers, retries and concurrent calls. Report a race only with an interleaving those callers can produce.

3. Keep going after the first defect until you have covered the whole diff.
4. Before you report a candidate, try to disprove it by reading the code: open the code it depends on, find the caller or input that triggers it, and check whether a guard elsewhere already prevents it. Drop it if you cannot show the path from the code.

Inspect with read-only commands (git, rg, reading files). Do not install dependencies or run builds or tests.

## What to report

Report a defect only when all of these hold:
- This Change introduced it. Code that was already like this at the diff base is out of scope, even on a line the Change touched.
- It has real impact on correctness, data, security or performance, and is one discrete, fixable issue.
- You can name the input, state or sequence that triggers it. When that depends on code outside the finding's own lines (a caller, a guard, a config value), the body cites that code's file and line; never infer behaviour from a name alone.
- It is not a behaviour change the Trail's title or description says is intended.
- Fixing it asks no more rigor than the surrounding code holds itself to, and the author would fix it if they knew.

Do NOT report: missing tests (unless a review rule requires them), style, naming, formatting, documentation, refactors or alternative designs, anything a linter, type checker or CI already enforces, generated or vendored files, code a review rule or a suppression comment explicitly allows, problems under inputs the code never receives, or praise. Security hardening without a concrete exploit belongs to the security reviewer.

## How to write findings

- One finding per distinct defect. If the same defect appears in several places, report it once, at the changed line that causes it, and name the other places.
- Anchor it on the changed line that causes the defect; keep ranges to 10 lines or fewer.
- Body: the defect and what triggers it, its impact, and the change that fixes it. One short paragraph, at most 3 lines of code, matter-of-fact.
- Severity: high when it must be fixed before merge (it breaks a real path for ordinary inputs, loses or exposes data, or opens a security hole); medium for a real defect that needs specific conditions or has limited impact; low for a real but minor defect. Never overstate it.
- Confidence: 0.9 or more when you traced the triggering path in the code; 0.7 to 0.9 with strong evidence and one assumption left; 0.5 to 0.7 when one condition could not be confirmed. Do not report anything below 0.5.
- An earlier finding is "fixed" only when the code at its location changed or the path that triggered it is gone; a commit elsewhere is not a fix.

* **Lens 2, Security Review:**

```text
Security Review

Review this change for security vulnerabilities it introduces or exposes: missing or bypassable authentication and authorization checks, privilege escalation and cross-tenant access; injection (SQL, shell command, path traversal, template); unsafe deserialization; secrets or credentials in code, logs or errors; insecure defaults; missing validation of untrusted input at a trust boundary; and exposure of data to callers who should not see it.

Trace untrusted input from where it enters to where it is used. Report only issues with a plausible exploit path through the changed code, and state the impact.

Do NOT report: general code quality, style, missing tests, or hardening suggestions without a concrete vulnerability.

The signal is true when you report at least one vulnerability, false when you report none.
```

```text

You are a very strict reviewer of agent-generated code slop. Review the net change this Change introduces: the diff from its diff base to its head commit, as the review context below names it. Judge the code, not who wrote it.

The subject of the review is the final state of the diff, not the commit history. Ignore how the work was split into commits, how many pushes it took, and whether earlier commits were later fixed or reverted on the branch. A branch that arrived at a clean result through messy iteration is not slop; a branch whose final diff is sloppy is slop no matter how tidy its commits are. Anything already at the diff base is existing code, not the subject of the review.

Work from the review context:

1. Start with the changed files and the patch in the review context. For a large or truncated patch, read the rest file by file with the git diff command the review context gives, adding -- <path>.
2. Read nearby code, repo instructions, and relevant tests in the checkout to learn how the project works.
3. You may skim the commit log from the diff base to the head commit to understand intent, but do not grade individual commits.

Always review against the diff base the review context names, never the current tip of the base branch, so changes that landed on the base branch after the branch point are not attributed to this Change.

This review is read-only against the repo's own tooling. Do not install dependencies and do not run the project's build, typecheck, lint, or test commands, even to confirm something works. Judge whether tests prove the new behavior by reading the test files and the code they exercise together, the same way you already read the diff. If a test's assertions don't match what the change claims to do, that is itself the finding.

Do not run `entire review`, use other AI agents, or hand off the review. Do it yourself with the repo and local checks.

Rate the amount of **Slop** the change adds as Low, Medium, or Large. Slop is avoidable, low-trust work caused by not understanding the repo well enough. It creates extra bugs, review work, or maintenance work.

First understand what the change is trying to do. Follow every workflow, route, state change, and rule it touches from start to finish. Read whether the tests prove the new behavior instead of only matching the code or new text.

Base the rating on:

1. **Severity** — How much can the problem break or burden?
2. **Prevalence** — How much of the change has the problem?
3. **Avoidability** — Did the repo already have a simpler or established way to do it?

Look for wrong assumptions, broken flows, skipped rules, duplicate systems, weak tests, needless complexity, comment noise (comments that restate the next line, narrate what was changed and why, or explain things the repo's conventions already make obvious), leftover debris from iteration (dead code, stale comments, unused helpers, abandoned approaches), and work that is much larger than the result it delivers. Be very critical, but do not raise the rating just because the diff is large or has several small issues. Do not call necessary complexity slop, and do not charge the change for problems it merely sits next to.

Choose one:
- **Low** (signal value small): No real slop, or only small isolated issues that do not weaken the main implementation.
- **Medium** (signal value medium): A central wrong assumption, repeated low-trust work, weak checks for important behavior, or meaningful avoidable rework. The implementation can still be fixed without replacing its core.
- **Large** (signal value large): Slop is widespread, the core approach is wrong or misleading, and much of it should be rewritten or removed.

Report the rating as the signal. Its rationale must name the two strongest reasons for the rating, using concrete behavior or architecture problems, not surface-level signals. Report each concrete slop problem behind the rating as a finding anchored to the changed code it concerns.

# Changelog

Notable changes to this repository are recorded here from 02/09/2026 onward.
Earlier work is verifiable in the commit history and in the closed pull
requests.

This repository is **not versioned**: it publishes the personal profile of
`lcv-leo` and the static site at lcv-leo.lcv.dev. It does not publish packages
or a numbered artifact. Entries are grouped by date rather than semantic
version. Dates are written `DD/MM/AAAA` in Brasília time (UTC−03:00).

## Unreleased

- Update Claude Code Action to v1.0.280 and Dependency Review Action to v5.0.1
  at their complete immutable release commit SHAs, preserving workflow inputs
  and permissions. Align the Claude Code Action MIT license link with its new
  pin; the bundled minimatch license change to ISC is approved under LCV-666.

- Correct the master text's Section 7.C intake-routing rule in `AGENTS.md` and
  `CLAUDE.md`: the exactly-one-Team-or-template invariant applies to addresses
  of type `team`, `template`, and `asks`; Linear's official documentation
  proves that `asksWeb` web-form addresses carry no Team/Template field by
  platform design (the form routes through its page and template, and the API
  refuses updates on them), so an `asksWeb` address with null team and null
  template is valid — never a finding or a pendency. This closes the external
  pendency that held the daily audits at PARTIAL since LCV-604, proven
  10/11/2026 under LCV-619.

- Align `.github/dependabot.yml` with the fleet standard: each `package-ecosystem`
  block keeps its `cooldown` configured (`default-days: 7`) but now excludes every
  dependency (`exclude: "*"`), so version updates are proposed immediately instead
  of observing the seven-day delay. The previous partial exclusion
  (`actions/*`, `github/*`) is replaced by the whole-ecosystem `*`, matching every
  organization repository and the master text's External Actions rule. The
  `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md` cooldown prose is corrected to the same
  wording, and `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` Section 7.A carries the corrected External
  Actions rule (LCV-619).

- Align the `THIRDPARTY.md` license link for the official CodeQL SARIF upload
  Action with its pinned v4.39.3 release commit SHA (LCV-574).

- Update the official CodeQL SARIF upload Action to v4.39.2 and Claude Code
  Action to v1.0.268 at their complete immutable release commit SHAs, preserving
  existing workflow inputs, permissions and separate CLI terms (LCV-554).

- Update the official Zizmor Action to v0.8.1 and its explicitly selected
  analyzer to 1.32.0 at their immutable release coordinates (LCV-542).

- Update the official Linear Release Action to v0.18.2 at its complete immutable
  release commit SHA, preserving the existing workflow inputs and official
  Linear CLI v0.18.0 (LCV-488; LCV-518).

- Enable native Google Antigravity CLI (`agy`) hooks in `.agents/hooks.json` and
  document the Antigravity integration and MCP configuration in `docs/entire.md`
  (LCV-477).

- Configure official Entire Brain/Graph guidance and the Codex MCP; document
  repository-specific merge gates, required branch freshness, removal of the
  retired Depot gate, and the remaining checkpoint/Trail evidence (LCV-477).
- Authenticate the `Claude Code` workflow to the Claude API by workload
  identity federation under its own Anthropic federation rule, which accepts
  only this repository: the job's GitHub OIDC token is exchanged for a
  short-lived Claude API token, and the workflow holds only identifiers. The
  repository secret `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` was deleted on 25/10/2026, so
  `SECURITY.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` no longer list it as a credential
  exception (LCVLEO-43, LCV-455).

- Add the `Claude Code` workflow (`.github/workflows/claude.yml`), an exact copy
  of the fleet's canonical file: the official `anthropics/claude-code-action`
  pinned by full commit SHA, inline review threads, commits signed through the
  GitHub API, no action on Dependabot pull requests, authenticated by the
  repository secret `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and the Claude GitHub App
  installed on the personal account. Add a reduced English `CLAUDE.md` for the
  GitHub Actions runtime, list the Action in `THIRDPARTY.md`, where the checkout
  row now states that only the Claude Code job keeps credentials, and record the
  second credential exception in `SECURITY.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` (LCVLEO-42,
  LCV-441).

- Ignore the operator-mandated repository-local `temp/` workspace so audit and
  test artifacts cannot be committed (LCV-414).

 Earlier work is verifiable in the commit history and in the closed pull
 requests.
 
 This repository is **not versioned**: it publishes the personal profile of
 `lcv-leo` and the static site at lcv-leo.lcv.dev. It does not publish packages
 or a numbered artifact. Entries are grouped by date rather than semantic
 version. Dates are written `DD/MM/AAAA` in Brasília time (UTC−03:00).
 
 ## Unreleased
 
 - Update Claude Code Action to v1.0.280 and Dependency Review Action to v5.0.1
   at their complete immutable release commit SHAs, preserving workflow inputs
   and permissions. Align the Claude Code Action MIT license link with its new
   pin; the bundled minimatch license change to ISC is approved under LCV-666.
 
 - Correct the master text's Section 7.C intake-routing rule in `AGENTS.md` and
   `CLAUDE.md`: the exactly-one-Team-or-template invariant applies to addresses
   of type `team`, `template`, and `asks`; Linear's official documentation
   proves that `asksWeb` web-form addresses carry no Team/Template field by
   platform design (the form routes through its page and template, and the API
   refuses updates on them), so an `asksWeb` address with null team and null
   template is valid — never a finding or a pendency. This closes the external
   pendency that held the daily audits at PARTIAL since LCV-604, proven
   10/11/2026 under LCV-619.
 
 - Align `.github/dependabot.yml` with the fleet standard: each `package-ecosystem`
   block keeps its `cooldown` configured (`default-days: 7`) but now excludes every
   dependency (`exclude: "*"`), so version updates are proposed immediately instead
   of observing the seven-day delay. The previous partial exclusion
   (`actions/*`, `github/*`) is replaced by the whole-ecosystem `*`, matching every
   organization repository and the master text's External Actions rule. The
   `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md` cooldown prose is corrected to the same
   wording, and `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` Section 7.A carries the corrected External
   Actions rule (LCV-619).
 
 - Align the `THIRDPARTY.md` license link for the official CodeQL SARIF upload
   Action with its pinned v4.39.3 release commit SHA (LCV-574).
 
 - Update the official CodeQL SARIF upload Action to v4.39.2 and Claude Code
   Action to v1.0.268 at their complete immutable release commit SHAs, preserving
   existing workflow inputs, permissions and separate CLI terms (LCV-554).
 
 - Update the official Zizmor Action to v0.8.1 and its explicitly selected
   analyzer to 1.32.0 at their immutable release coordinates (LCV-542).
 
 - Update the official Linear Release Action to v0.18.2 at its complete immutable
   release commit SHA, preserving the existing workflow inputs and official
   Linear CLI v0.18.0 (LCV-488; LCV-518).
 
 - Enable native Google Antigravity CLI (`agy`) hooks in `.agents/hooks.json` and
   document the Antigravity integration and MCP configuration in `docs/entire.md`
   (LCV-477).
 
 - Configure official Entire Brain/Graph guidance and the Codex MCP; document
   repository-specific merge gates, required branch freshness, removal of the
   retired Depot gate, and the remaining checkpoint/Trail evidence (LCV-477).
 - Authenticate the `Claude Code` workflow to the Claude API by workload
   identity federation under its own Anthropic federation rule, which accepts
   only this repository: the job's GitHub OIDC token is exchanged for a
   short-lived Claude API token, and the workflow holds only identifiers. The
   repository secret `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` was deleted on 25/10/2026, so
   `SECURITY.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` no longer list it as a credential
   exception (LCVLEO-43, LCV-455).
 
 - Add the `Claude Code` workflow (`.github/workflows/claude.yml`), an exact copy
   of the fleet's canonical file: the official `anthropics/claude-code-action`
   pinned by full commit SHA, inline review threads, commits signed through the
   GitHub API, no action on Dependabot pull requests, authenticated by the
   repository secret `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and the Claude GitHub App
   installed on the personal account. Add a reduced English `CLAUDE.md` for the
   GitHub Actions runtime, list the Action in `THIRDPARTY.md`, where the checkout
   row now states that only the Claude Code job keeps credentials, and record the
   second credential exception in `SECURITY.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` (LCVLEO-42,
   LCV-441).
 
 - Ignore the operator-mandated repository-local `temp/` workspace so audit and
   test artifacts cannot be committed (LCV-414).

móvel do portfólio — Kotlin, Android, Jetpack Compose e Gradle com ícones
  próprios, e Material 3, Hilt, Room e Retrofit/OkHttp como selos. A
  **Calculadora Android** aparece com a v1.0.0 publicada na Google Play, motor
  de cálculo em Kotlin puro, sem rastreamento, sem anúncio e sem conta; as
  edições Android do Astrólogo e do Maestro constam como iniciadas. Os quatro
  ícones novos foram vendorizados do mesmo commit fixado do Devicon já em uso,
  com seus SHA-256 registrados no inventário. O Gradle entra como selo, e não
  como ícone: o `gradle-original.svg` é `#02303a` e fica ilegível sobre o fundo
  escuro tanto da página quanto do README em tema escuro — medido na
  renderização, não suposto (LCV-203).

### Fixed

- O Contribution Graph do README voltou a renderizar: o cartão passou a ser
  gerado neste repositório a partir do calendário oficial da API GraphQL do
  GitHub e servido por `lcv-leo.lcv.dev`, no lugar do endpoint público do
  GitHub Readme Activity Graph, desativado pelo provedor (HTTP 402
  `DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED`). A página `lcv-leo.lcv.dev` acompanhou a troca, e a
  CSP derivada deixou de admitir o host desativado (LCV2-27).

- Removida a referência obsoleta a fsevents do inventário de desenvolvimento;
  o lockfile atual do Playwright não contém esse pacote.

### Changed

- Update the official Linear Release Action to v0.18.1 at its full commit SHA,
  select the official CLI v0.18.0 explicitly and retain upstream checksum
  verification (LCV-316).

- Dependabot verifica GitHub Actions e npm todos os dias, inclusive fins de
  semana, às 05h, e agrupa as correções de segurança separadamente por ecossistema.
- Atualizado o pin oficial do zizmor-action para v0.8.0, com o SHA completo da
  respectiva release e o inventário de terceiros atual reconciliado (LCV-438).

## 09/09/2026 — Mídia do perfil hospedada no próprio repositório (LCV2-24)

### Changed

- Os cinco GIFs e os 13 ícones Devicon usados no perfil agora têm cópias locais
  byte a byte, com referências ao próprio repositório; o Pages usa os ícones
  locais. As animações, a composição e as dimensões foram preservadas.
- Fontes, contadores, estatísticas, gráficos, badges e demais serviços dinâmicos

- O cartão dinâmico de detalhes do README exibe `lcv-leo (LCV)` usando o
  parâmetro oficial `name` do provedor, evitando o corte do nome. O nome do
  perfil GitHub e o título equivalente no Pages não foram alterados.
- Incluídos os textos MIT originais do Devicon e do catálogo dos GIFs, com
  créditos, fontes e hashes em THIRDPARTY; a declaração do catálogo não foi
  apresentada como comprovação de autoria individual das animações.
- Ajustados somente o inventário de mídia, a política de imagens do Pages e
  a descrição do teste de proveniência correspondente.
- O teste existente de retry usa `Clock.pauseAt` do Playwright e aguarda o
  agendamento antes de verificar o limite de 2.500 ms, sem alterar a lógica
  do site ou relaxar as asserções.

## 02/09/2026 — Governança nativa do repositório ([#51](https://github.com/lcv-leo/lcv-leo/issues/51), LCV2-21)

### Removed

- O lockfile `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, os passos de instalação e
  verificação do `gh-actions-lock` no workflow `Deploy Pages` e os cabeçalhos
  "managed by gh actions-lock": o padrão da organização deixou de usar lockfile
  de Actions.
- O workflow `codeql.yml`, substituído pelo default setup do code scanning do
  GitHub.
- O teste `scripts/linear-release-trust.test.mjs` e, em
  `scripts/provenance-drift.test.mjs`, os testes que validavam a forma dos

- Os badges "Merge Queues", "Merge queue ALLGREEN" e "actions.lock + SHA pins"
  do perfil, e as menções a merge queue e ao lockfile no perfil e no site.

### Added

- `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml`, o padrão da organização para

  segredo do Dependabot (`DEPENDABOT_AUTOMERGE_TOKEN`).
- `.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `INBOUND.md`
  e este `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Changed

- `dependabot.yml` semanal (segunda-feira, 06:00 em Brasília) com um grupo de
  minor e patch por ecossistema, majors separados, labels, prefixo e rebase

- `zizmor.yml` alinhado ao exemplo oficial (zizmor-action v0.6.3, agenda
  semanal); `scorecard.yml` só com push em `main` e agenda semanal;
  `linear-release.yml` com linear-release-action v0.17.2, mantendo o gatilho
  `workflow_run` em `Deploy Pages` e `command: sync`; `Deploy Pages` com
  deploy-pages v5.0.1, Node.js 24 e o job de deploy restrito a `main`.

  grafo de dependências do GitHub como inventário versionado, e mantém as seções
  legais de fontes, ícones, mídia hospedada e serviços externos.

result.content:
# Third-party components

This inventory covers every external GitHub Action invoked by the repository
workflows, the CI-only npm and browser validation tooling, and the externally
hosted components used by the profile or the Pages site. The repository's
package manifest contains only development tooling for browser-level
provenance tests. No npm package, browser binary, or FFmpeg binary is copied
into `site/` or the deployed GitHub Pages artifact; the site's committed
JavaScript uses browser built-ins and GitHub APIs.

The versioned inventory is the repository's **dependency graph** (Insights →
Dependency graph), which GitHub maintains from the committed manifest, lockfile
and workflow files and exports as an SBOM on request. Versions, version ranges
and immutable commit pins live only in `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, the
workflow files and `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, where Dependabot updates
them; this document deliberately does not repeat them, so it can never drift
from those sources. The GitHub Actions dependency lockfile
(`actions.lock`, generated by `gh actions-lock --no-narrow` and never edited by
hand) additionally pins the transitive Actions that no workflow file references
and records each source repository's identity
([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles)).
The official GitHub
Dependency Review action evaluates manifest and lockfile changes on every pull
request to `main`, and the Pages workflow installs the committed lockfile with lifecycle
scripts disabled.

The repository's original content is proprietary and all rights are reserved.
The licenses below apply only to their respective third-party components.

## GitHub Actions

Every external Action is pinned to an immutable commit SHA in the workflows, as
the repository's Actions policy requires. Tooling that an Action selects at
runtime (the Linear CLI, the zizmor tool and Scorecard image, the CodeQL bundle
used by code scanning, the `oven-sh/setup-bun` step that the Claude Code Action
runs) is governed by that Action's own release and license; the Claude Code
software itself has its own license, noted below the table.

| Component                          | License                                                                      | Source                                              | Purpose                                                     |

2. **Lockfiles:** as Section 6.B requires. GitHub Actions dependency lockfiles exist and are generally available: `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, generated only by the `gh actions-lock` CLI extension and never edited by hand, refreshed automatically by Dependabot inside the same version-update pull request ([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles), [Locking action dependencies](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/lock-workflow-dependencies)). **Fleet position (operator decision, 25/11/2026):** every repository adopts the Actions lockfile **and keeps its `uses:` references pinned to a full-length commit SHA with the version comment**. GitHub checks the locked commit for an onboarded workflow and a lockfile satisfies the SHA-pinning policy by itself, so the in-file SHA is the fleet's reviewed record, not the enforcement point; keep it so the reviewed pin survives deletion of the lockfile and stays readable in review ([Governing execution of GitHub Actions workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/administer/control-workflow-execution#require-lockfile)). Generate and refresh with **`gh actions-lock --no-narrow`**; a plain run rewrites the pins to version tags and is forbidden here. The **Require lockfile** policy exists at the enterprise in **Evaluate** mode: under Policy insights it records the workflow runs that **Active** mode would block; move it to **Active** only after every targeted repository passes `gh actions-lock --verify` (same page). The extension locks external actions and the actions a `$/` path uses. A local path action (`uses: ./…`) runs whatever is checked out in the runner's workspace, so the extension can neither pin it nor see what it uses. When such an action uses other actions, the extension stops with a `local-action` error before writing the lockfile, so take one of the two documented decisions — `--migrate-local-actions`, which rewrites the reference to the inherently pinned `uses: $/…` form, or an explicit `--ignore-local-actions` — and record which one in the pull request ([Locking action dependencies](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/lock-workflow-dependencies)). A `$/` path runs at the workflow's own commit and is pinned by that commit. A routine `--no-narrow` change touches `actions.lock` only, but upstream renames and transfers rewrite `uses:` names and `--migrate-local-actions` edits workflows, so read the full diff. Every lockfile change still sweeps all eight surfaces of this section. The lockfile does not cover reusable-workflow calls (`jobs.<job_id>.uses`): a cross-repository call stays pinned by full commit SHA, while a same-repository `$/` or `./` call carries no `@ref` and runs at the caller's own commit ([Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax)). A Wrangler update also regenerates `worker-configuration.d.ts` under the Section 3 exception and commits it before pushing.

unknown flag: --repo

Makes an authenticated HTTP request to the GitHub API and prints the response.

The endpoint argument should either be a path of a GitHub API v3 endpoint, or
`graphql` to access the GitHub API v4.

Placeholder values `{owner}`, `{repo}`, and `{branch}` in the endpoint
argument will get replaced with values from the repository of the current
directory or the repository specified in the `GH_REPO` environment variable.
Note that in some shells, for example PowerShell, you may need to enclose
any value that contains `{...}` in quotes to prevent the shell from
applying special meaning to curly braces.

The `-p/--preview` flag enables opting into previews, which are feature-flagged,
experimental API endpoints or behaviors. The API expects opt-in via the `Accept`
header with format `application/vnd.github.<preview-name>-preview+json` and this
command facilitates that via `--preview <preview-name>`. To send a request for
the corsair and scarlet witch previews, you could use `-p corsair,scarlet-witch`
or `--preview corsair --preview scarlet-witch`.

The default HTTP request method is `GET` normally and `POST` if any parameters
were added. Override the method with `--method`.

Pass one or more `-f/--raw-field` values in `key=value` format to add static string
parameters to the request payload. To add non-string or placeholder-determined values, see
`-F/--field` below. Note that adding request parameters will automatically switch the
request method to `POST`. To send the parameters as a `GET` query string instead, use
`--method GET`.

The `-F/--field` flag has magic type conversion based on the format of the value:

- literal values `true`, `false`, `null`, and integer numbers get converted to
  appropriate JSON types;
- placeholder values `{owner}`, `{repo}`, and `{branch}` get populated with values
  from the repository of the current directory;
- if the value starts with `@`, the rest of the value is interpreted as a
  filename to read the value from. Pass `-` to read from standard input.

For GraphQL requests, all fields other than `query` and `operationName` are
interpreted as GraphQL variables.

To pass nested parameters in the request payload, use `key[subkey]=value` syntax when
declaring fields. To pass nested values as arrays, declare multiple fields with the
syntax `key[]=value1`, `key[]=value2`. To pass an empty array, use `key[]` without a
value.

To pass pre-constructed JSON or payloads in other formats, a request body may be read
from file specified by `--input`. Use `-` to read from standard input. When passing the
request body this way, any parameters specified via field flags are added to the query
string of the endpoint URL.

In `--paginate` mode, all pages of results will sequentially be requested until
there are no more pages of results. For GraphQL requests, this requires that the
original query accepts an `$endCursor: String` variable and that it fetches the
`pageInfo{ hasNextPage, endCursor }` set of fields from a collection. Each page is a separate
JSON array or object. Pass `--slurp` to wrap all pages of JSON arrays or objects
into an outer JSON array.

For more information about output formatting flags, see `gh help formatting`.

USAGE
  gh api <endpoint> [flags]

FLAGS
      --allow-escape-sequences[=true|false]   Allow printing terminal escape sequences
      --cache duration                        Cache the response, e.g. "3600s", "60m", "1h"
  -F, --field key=value                       Add a typed parameter in key=value format (use "@<path>" or "@-" to read value from file or stdin)
  -H, --header key:value                      Add a HTTP request header in key:value format
      --hostname string                       The GitHub hostname for the request (default "github.com")
  -i, --include[=true|false]                  Include HTTP response status line and headers in the output
      --input file                            The file to use as body for the HTTP request (use "-" to read from standard input)
  -q, --jq string                             Query to select values from the response using jq syntax
  -X, --method string                         The HTTP method for the request (default "GET")
      --paginate[=true|false]                 Make additional HTTP requests to fetch all pages of results
  -p, --preview strings                       Opt into GitHub API previews (names should omit '-preview')
  -f, --raw-field key=value                   Add a string parameter in key=value format
      --silent[=true|false]                   Do not print the response body
      --slurp[=true|false]                    Use with "--paginate" to return an array of all pages of either JSON arrays or objects
  -t, --template string                       Format JSON output using a Go template; see "gh help formatting"
      --verbose[=true|false]                  Include full HTTP request and response in the output

INHERITED FLAGS
  --help[=true|false]   Show help for command

EXAMPLES
  # List releases in the current repository
  $ gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases
  
  # Post an issue comment
  $ gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/123/comments -f body='Hi from CLI'
  
  # Post nested parameter read from a file
  $ gh api gists -F 'files[myfile.txt][content]=@myfile.txt'
  
  # Add parameters to a GET request
  $ gh api -X GET search/issues -f q='repo:cli/cli is:open remote'
  
  # Use a JSON file as request body
  $ gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets --input file.json
  
  # Set a custom HTTP header
  $ gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.v3.raw+json' ...
  
  # Opt into GitHub API previews
  $ gh api --preview baptiste,nebula ...
  
  # Print only specific fields from the response
  $ gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues --jq '.[].title'
  
  # Use a template for the output
  $ gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues --template \
    '{{range .}}{{.title}} ({{.labels | pluck "name" | join ", " | color "yellow"}}){{"\n"}}{{end}}'
  
  # Update allowed values of the "environment" custom property in a deeply nested array
  $ gh api -X PATCH /orgs/{org}/properties/schema \
     -F 'properties[][property_name]=environment' \
     -F 'properties[][default_value]=production' \
     -F 'properties[][allowed_values][]=staging' \
     -F 'properties[][allowed_values][]=production'
  
  # List releases with GraphQL
  $ gh api graphql -F owner='{owner}' -F name='{repo}' -f query='
    query($name: String!, $owner: String!) {
      repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) {
        releases(last: 3) {
          nodes { tagName }
        }
      }
    }
  '
  
  # List all repositories for a user
  $ gh api graphql --paginate -f query='
    query($endCursor: String) {
      viewer {
        repositories(first: 100, after: $endCursor) {
          nodes { nameWithOwner }
          pageInfo {
            hasNextPage
            endCursor
          }
        }
      }
    }
  '
  
  # Get the percentage of forks for the current user
  $ gh api graphql --paginate --slurp -f query='
    query($endCursor: String) {
      viewer {
        repositories(first: 100, after: $endCursor) {
          nodes { isFork }
          pageInfo {
            hasNextPage
            endCursor
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ' | jq 'def count(e): reduce e as $_ (0;.+1);
  [.[].data.viewer.repositories.nodes[]] as $r | count(select($r[].isFork))/count($r[])'

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
  GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN (in order of precedence): an authentication token for
  API requests to `github.com`, a subdomain of `ghe.com`, or `github.localhost`.
  
  GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN (in order of precedence): an
  authentication token for API requests to GitHub Enterprise Server. `gh` treats
  any host other than `github.com`, a subdomain of `ghe.com`, or
  `github.localhost` as a GitHub Enterprise Server host.
  
  GH_HOST: make the request to a GitHub host other than `github.com`.

LEARN MORE
  Use `gh <command> <subcommand> --help` for more information about a command.
  Read the manual at https://cli.github.com/manual
  Learn about exit codes using `gh help exit-codes`
  Learn about accessibility experiences using `gh help accessibility`
